title: Agricultural Equipment Operators
aliases: Agricultural and Horticultural Mobile Plant Operator

claims.text: Adoption of autonomous and semi-autonomous machinery among Australian grain growers rose from 27% to 45% between the first (2024) and second (results published April 2026) waves of a national survey by Grain Producers Australia, the Tractor and Machinery Association of Australia and the Society of Precision Agriculture Australia, with tractors and sprayers the most common entry point and grower interest in learning more rising to 69%.

sources.title: Autonomous Farm Machinery | Code of Practice and survey snapshot
sources.whatItMeasured: Second-wave survey of 200+ Australian grain producers (Autonomous Farm Machinery use in Australia - a snapshot 2026): adoption share, entry-point machine types, learning preferences

sources.title: Autonomous farm machinery uptake caught between interest and adoption realities
sources.whatItMeasured: Peak-body release confirming cost, return on investment and regional connectivity as primary adoption barriers

claims.scope: Grain producers (broadacre cropping) nationally. 'Adoption' includes semi-autonomous functions such as autosteer guidance, not only fully driverless machines, and is self-reported. Says nothing directly about operator employment levels.
claims.refuteNotes: Lens 1 (source real): peak body's own site, both pages resolve 200, post carries datePublished 2026-05-05, results stated as published April 2026. Lens 2 (population fit): grain growers, which is where this occupation's automation exposure is concentrated; horticulture covered separately by c03. Lens 3 (in window): April-May 2026, inside window. No refuter overturned.

claims.text: A Code of Practice for Agricultural Mobile Field Machinery with Autonomous Functions in Australia, developed by Grain Producers Australia with the Tractor and Machinery Association and the Society of Precision Agriculture Australia, guides safe work procedures for semi-autonomous and autonomous mobile field machinery used in planting, spraying, fertilising and harvesting in grain production systems.

sources.title: Autonomous Farm Machinery | Code of Practice
sources.whatItMeasured: Industry code of practice scope statement and development history (development from 2019, released July 2021 per page updates)

claims.scope: Voluntary industry code, not statute or regulation; compliance is not legally enforceable as written here. Grain production systems are its stated focus. It is the closest instrument to a governing standard for autonomous field machinery, so WHS duties under the model Act still apply alongside it.
claims.refuteNotes: Lens 1: primary page resolves 200 with dated update history. Lens 2: covers the machine classes this occupation operates. Lens 3: standing instrument predating the window; retained as L1 context per the plan's freshness rule. Dissent: it is industry-led rather than statutory, so the tier records exactly that.

claims.text: Hort Innovation and the Almond Board of Australia ran a completed demonstration project (AS17002, Demonstration of functional driverless tractor for Australian horticulture) trialling a retrofitted driverless tractor with remote monitoring in Australian almond orchards; the technology contractor linked grower interest to difficulty staffing tractor seats, including night shifts.

sources.title: AS17002 - Demonstration of functional driverless tractor for Australian horticulture (project register)
sources.whatItMeasured: Grower-funded R&D register entry recording AS17002 as a completed project (page undated; retrieved 2026-08-26)

sources.title: Driverless tractor trial on track
sources.whatItMeasured: Trade report of the trial's GOtrack retrofit, remote monitoring app, demonstration days, and AME Group commentary that staffing tractor seats including night shifts was getting harder (article undated; approximate date flagged)

claims.scope: One horticultural trial in almonds. Demonstrates technical feasibility and employer motivation, not displacement of operators at scale. The quoted contractor commentary comes from an undated trade article and should be re-dated before print use.
claims.refuteNotes: Lens 1: Hort Innovation register resolves 200; treecrop page resolves 200 but publishes no dateline, so one refuter overturned on dating grounds. Lens 2: population fit for horticulture operators. Lens 3: project completion date uncertain; claim survives two-to-one with the dating dissent carried into scope.

jobAds.query: farm machinery operator (113 results); plant operator agriculture (13 results)
jobAds.notes: Precision-technology keywords are nearly absent from ad text (autosteer/GPS/guidance <=1 mention across 126 listings), despite c01 showing 45% adoption of autonomous or semi-autonomous machinery among growers. Ads describe conventional operating skills; demand for precision-tech operator skills is not yet visible in ad language.

caveats: High confidence rests on the L1/L2 core (peak-body survey plus code of practice); the declared L5 corpus contained zero items from Australian machinery operators, so practitioner-discourse signals are absent rather than negative.
'agricultural equipment operator' as a title barely appears in the Australian market; ads use 'farm machinery operator' and 'mobile plant operator'.
